newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Trend shows small rise in NZ Sept qtr retail data.
newsitem.headline: Trend shows small rise in NZ Sept qtr retail data.

text.p: The underlying trend in New Zealand retail sales showed a slight increase in the September month and the September quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday.
The trend showed a 0.1 percent increase in September and a 0.2 percent rise in the September quarter.
This was despite seasonally adjusted real figures showing sales fell 0.3 percent in the quarter -- in line with economists' forecasts of a 0.4 percent fall.
During the quarter the government introduced the first half of a NZ$3 billion tax cut package. There was also a general election held on October 12.
Actual sales in the year rose 2.9 percent against forecasts of a 2.5 percent rise.

The food group contributed 40 percent of the total annual increase with sales up $108 million. The motor vehicles group and cafe, restaurant and takeaway groups were the other groups to record significant rises. Ten of the 15 store types posted gains.
Retail sales for the month of September increased 2.4 percent from September 1995.
